teaser: Lovable with SHarness, and the trojanised Claude Code extension: where a policy boundary has to sit, and what SHarness can stop today.
core_idea: A tampered Claude Code extension in Cursor's marketplace ran on load with the editor's permissions, tried an SSH backdoor and persistence, and sent the machine's details out; the agent did not misbehave, the host was backdoored. A Process Behaviour Policy has a row refusing each step, and the file and network rows run today in SHarness, but only on Linux and not yet around an editor, so it would not have stopped this. Lovable builds in its cloud, beyond SHarness, but its two-way Git sync brings the local work into a SHarness shell that writes only the workspace and reaches only named sites, while production secrets stay in Lovable.
